questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why it rains so much in Britain
How scientists predict the weather
Scientific ways to change the weather
How floods damage farmers' crops
questions.why: Sam says they'll hear about cloud-seeding and geo-engineering, methods to change the weather.

questions.q: Why is Sam's news disappointing for Neil?
options: The methods make more rain, not less
The methods are far too expensive
The methods only work in hot countries
The methods don't work at all in Britain
questions.why: She says, 'these ideas involve making more, not less, rain'.

options: Mirrors reflect sunlight away from clouds
Machines on the ground blow clouds away
Water is pumped up into the sky from lakes
Planes spray chemicals to make snowflakes
questions.why: Airplanes spray chemicals to make water particles freeze and stick together as snowflakes.

questions.q: How does Professor Katja Friedrich answer people who say cloud seeding puts unnatural substances in the air?
options: She agrees and has stopped her research
Cars and planes also put things in the air
She says the substances are completely natural
She says only a few countries use it now
questions.why: She says every time you drive or fly you put substances in the air, so 'you're also playing God'.

questions.q: What is special about solar geo-engineering compared with cloud seeding?
options: It is already used in over fifty countries
It makes more snow fall in the mountains
It has never been tested; it's a theory
It started in the 1940s in America
questions.why: Neil says it has never been tested and is still just a theory.

questions.q: Why are people scared of solar geo-engineering, according to Professor David Keith?
options: It gives countries an excuse not to cut emissions
It could make the Earth far too cold to live on
It could stop airplanes from flying safely
It is too expensive for poor countries to use
questions.why: He says it could provide an excuse to avoid doing the work needed to cut emissions.

questions.q: How has the controversy about geo-engineering changed over time?
options: It has always been a taboo subject for scientists
It was normal to discuss, then became taboo
It was taboo in the 1960s but is accepted now
Nobody discussed it at all until very recently
questions.why: He says in early work these ideas were just part of the discussion, but by the 90s and 2000s there was a taboo.

questions.q: What does Neil joke would be good for Britain?
options: Moving everyone to India
More cloud seeding over London
A giant mirror in space to cool it
A giant floating umbrella above it
questions.why: He says a giant floating umbrella above Britain would be good.
